setup.summary: Solar $setup now preserves native AutoSci setup semantics as an approval-gated route: it reads the setup guide/env template, detects provider-key readiness without recording secrets, reports Python/venv status, keeps .env writes blocked by default, and recognizes approved external setup runtime evidence for user-directed credential/configuration changes.

acceptance_checks.detail: Solar setup route has a local setup guide and env template matching the native role of explaining optional source/review provider configuration.
The setup status smoke detected provider key readiness, Python executable/version, .env presence, and .venv presence and archived autosci_setup_status.v1.
Regression coverage and the setup smoke verify that setup records key names and booleans only; dummy secret values were not serialized into run artifacts.
Default $setup remains proposal/status evidence only and does not mutate .env, wiki, tools, or runtime paths.
Approved external setup runtime evidence is recognized through approval and side-effect proof manifests; local secret/config mutation remains blocked unless explicitly user-approved.
Targeted setup/control tests cover gated execution status, workflow gate compatibility, setup status artifact emission, Review LLM readiness booleans, and secret redaction.

findings.finding: The setup route is semantically full as an approval-gated route: status detection is native and non-mutating by default, while credential writes remain approval/runtime-evidence governed.
No setup evidence stores credential values; only key names, booleans, paths, and readiness summaries are serialized.
